children: The greenfield multimodal logistics hub in Greater Noida will be developed in three phases with a planned capacity of 1.44 million TEUs and 7.8 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, JSW Infrastructure and Essar Ports have submitted initial bids for a Rs 5,881 crore greenfield Multi Modal Logistics Hub (MMLH) at Dadri in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

The tender has been floated by DMIC Integrated Industrial Township Greater Noida, a special-purpose vehicle formed by the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) and the Greater Noida Development Authority (GNIDA). This marks the second attempt in the past year to develop the large-scale logistics facility.
Spread across 311 hectares, the logistics hub will provide mechanised warehousing, specialised storage, cargo handling and intermodal transfer facilities for containerised, bulk and break-bulk cargo.

The project will be developed in three phases over a 45-year concession period. The first phase entails an investment of Rs 2,374 crore and will provide capacity to handle 0.74 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and 6.7 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo.

The second phase, involving Rs 1,412 crore, will increase capacity to 1.12 million TEUs and 7.2 million tonnes of non-containerised cargo. The final phase, requiring Rs 2,095 crore, will take capacity to 1.44 million TEUs and 7.8 million tonnes.

The facility will also include modern warehousing and cold storage infrastructure. The private developer will create 3 million sq ft of warehousing space and 0.3 million sq ft of cold storage capacity in the first phase.

Warehousing capacity can subsequently rise to 4 million sq ft and 5.5 million sq ft in the second and third phases, respectively, while cold storage capacity is planned to increase to 0.4 million sq ft and 0.5 million sq ft.
The hub will also offer value-added services such as cross-docking, customisation, stacking and labelling.

The Dadri project is positioned at the junction of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors, giving it access to major freight routes connecting northern India with ports and industrial centres.

The facility will also have direct connectivity to NH34, the Eastern Peripheral Expressway and Jewar International Airport. It is located adjacent to the Delhi-Howrah broad-gauge railway line and old NH-91.

The location is expected to enable the hub to tap freight traffic on both dedicated freight corridors and support industrial and distribution activity across the National Capital Region and its hinterland.
Bidder To Be Selected On Revenue Share
The project will be awarded to the bidder offering the highest Minimum Guaranteed Revenue Share to the project authority.

The private concessionaire will be responsible for developing, operating, maintaining and managing the logistics hub, including its commercial and ancillary facilities. The project is expected to strengthen multimodal freight movement and improve logistics efficiency in the Greater Noida-Dadri industrial belt.
